statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-69439 (GHSA-527h-q9f6-p7qx) is an elevation of privilege issue in Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native, the native Windows library that reads program database (PDB) files: an out of bounds write can occur when parsing a Portable PDB file. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and the Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native package as the affected .NET 8 package, fixed in 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2, and lists the CVE in the .NET 8.0.31 release notes (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-527h-q9f6-p7qx, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/438, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.31/8.0.31.md). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux (linux-musl) from Microsoft's source release. Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold. No Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native file or package is present: none of the packages contains a native Windows PE file or a Mach-O file (every PE file in them is a managed .NET assembly), so the native Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native.*.dll libraries are absent. The packages do carry the separate, managed Microsoft.DiaSymReader library (2.1.0-beta.23253.1, a netstandard2.0 assembly in the dotnet-format and dotnet-watch tools and in Microsoft.DiaSymReader nupkg files), which defines the symbol reader interfaces and does not contain the native PDB parser. So the vulnerable code is not in this owner.

CVE-2026-69439 (GHSA-527h-q9f6-p7qx) is an elevation of privilege issue in Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native: an out-of-bounds write can occur when parsing a Portable PDB file. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and the Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native NuGet package (17.12.0-beta1.24603.5 through 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1, fixed in 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2) as the only affected .NET 9 package (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-527h-q9f6-p7qx, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/438, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.20/9.0.20.md). Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native consists of native Windows DLLs. DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. None of them contains a Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native file or nupkg, and none contains a native Windows PE file; every PE file in them is a managed .NET assembly. The managed Microsoft.DiaSymReader library (version 2.2.0-beta.24327.2) is present in the dotnet-format and dotnet-watch tools of the SDK held by dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap and as Microsoft.DiaSymReader nupkg files in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts; it is a separate package that Microsoft does not list as affected. So the vulnerable native component is not in this owner.
